To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the weak‐strong interaction can be treated by a perturbation scheme that uses a new kind of averaging (averaging over the weak beam) and that the resulting tune diagram has a structure that can be understood qualitatively and quantitatively.
the weak‐strong kick lattice map has an invariant torus, that the invariant torus is stable, and that the invariant tori can be used to approximate the dynamics in a region near the tori.

weak‐strong beam beam interactions in a kick‐lattice model can be approximated by a perturbation series that is valid in the entire tune diagram, and that this perturbation series can be used to obtain rigorous error bounds on our approximations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and implementation of perturbation theory and the use of the resulting approximations to study the weak‐strong and strong‐strong beam—beam interactions in the context of the beam‐beam kick lattice map.

understanding the dynamics in tune space, and we have found a new approach that allows one to obtain rigorous results in the vicinity of certain resonant surfaces, as well as to understand the global structure of the phase space in tune space.

the development of a perturbation theory for the kick‐map in two degrees of free‐dom (4‐d), which is a model for beam‐beam interactions, and its application to weak‐strong and strong‐strong beam beam.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach provides a rigorous and systematic method for analyzing beam–beam interactions.
our perturbation scheme is the first one to be fully rigorous and to yield a complete description of the dynamics.
the weak‐strong interaction is a very complicated phenomenon, but that our approach gives a systematic method of understanding its behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weak‐strong interaction is integrable in a certain sense, but that the integrability breaks down near resonances.
we have found a new class of perturbations that are valid over a large region of tune space, and which are valid even when the perturbation is large.
, in the weak‐strong regime (i.e., when the strong beam is small), the dynamics is well approximated by an averaging scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the beam‐beam interaction is integrable in the sense of Arnold (and not KAM).
the kick‐lattices are not integrable, and that the beam‐beam problem is not a perturbation of an integrable system.
the weak‐strong limit of the beam‐beam interaction is not a good model for the strong‐strong limit, but that it is a good model for a certain region of the strong‐strong tune diagram.
